title: Choosing the Right Chart Type
intro: Decide what the reader should understand, then pick the chart.

learn.title: Four purposes
learn.text:
**Distribution** — how values spread: histogram, heatmap, bubble, candlestick
**Composition** — what the whole is made of: pie or donut for a few parts, treemap, 100% stacked bar, waterfall
**Comparison** — bigger or smaller: bar, ordered bar for ranking, combination charts
**Relationship** — do measures move together: scatterplot

Then one extra question: **does change over time matter?** If so, favour line, multiline or stacked area.

try.q: You want readers to see which regions sold most. Which purpose is that?
try.explain: An ordered bar chart ranks them directly.

left.label: Ask first
items: Does the path matter, or the snapshot?

learn.title: Time is the extra question
learn.text:
The four purposes get you most of the way. Then ask whether the reader needs **the path, not just the snapshot**.

If they do, move to a line, multiline or stacked area chart. If they don't, a bar chart usually reads faster.

try.q: Readers need to see how a metric got to today's value. What does that call for?
try.explain: They need the path, not just the snapshot.

learn.title: Use the simple chart
learn.text:
Scatterplots show relationships — and correlation is not causation.

Use **tables** when readers need exact numbers.

And the rule that saves the most time: **if a simple bar chart answers the question, use the bar chart.**

try.q: When should you use a table instead of a chart?
options: When there are more than five categories
try.explain: A chart shows shape; a table gives values.

test.q: Which chart shows whether two measures move together?
test.explain: And correlation is still not causation.

test.q: Which purpose does a treemap serve?
test.explain: What the whole is made of.

test.q: What is the article's default advice?
options: Use the bar chart if it answers the question
Use a line chart for most metrics
Match the chart to the design system
test.explain: Simplicity beats sophistication when both work.
